Russian medical university
The Saratov State Medical University (SSMU; Russian: Саратовский государственный медицинский университет им. В. И. Разумовского, lit. 'Saratov State Medical University named after V.I. Razumovsky'; also known as Razumovsky University) is a public university located in Saratov, Russia.[1][2]

The university was founded in 1909 as Imperial University by the Decree of Emperor Nicholas II.[3] On June 10, 1909, the Emperor signed the "Decree on the foundation of the university in Saratov", which became the tenth University in Russia and consisted of the Medical Faculty only. Professor V.I. Razumovsky became the first university rector.[4] In 1930, the Medical Faculty of Saratov University was transformed into an independent institution of higher education, which was known as the Medical Institute.
In 1993, it received the status of a Medical University. In 2009, the university was named after its first rector Vasily Ivanovich Razumovsky.[5]

value.text:
Saratov State Medical University is a public university in Saratov, Russia, also known as Razumovsky University. Its Russian name commemorates Vasily Ivanovich Razumovsky, the first rector of the university from which it traces its origins. The institution is associated with the Ministry of Healthcare of the Russian Federation. Its listed teaching languages are Russian and English. The academic structure includes general medicine, pediatrics, dentistry, medical and preventative care, pharmacy and clinical psychology, together with a nursing institute and a faculty concerned with vocational training and professional retraining. Its motto translates as “Knowledge and heritage.”

The university traces its history to the Imperial University established in Saratov by decree of Nicholas II in 1909. At its foundation, that university consisted only of a medical faculty. In 1930 the medical faculty of Saratov University became an independent institution of higher education, known as the Medical Institute. The institution received medical university status in 1993 and was named after Razumovsky in 2009. The English-language rector list identifies Andrey Vyacheslavovich Eremin as serving from September 2020. These stages distinguish the university’s historical origin from the establishment of an independent medical institution and its later university designation.
